subject.title: Feature Request: Masked Secrets - Prevent Agent from Accessing Raw API Keys

question: Which supported first boundary should OpenClaw adopt for credentials used by agent-triggered work: extend the scoped broker from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98707, define a narrower agent-exec capability contract, or retain external isolation/plugin mitigations only?
rationale: Current main confirms the exposure remains for plaintext in agent-inspectable files, while the open broker deliberately limits itself to declared plugin operations. Selecting the security guarantee, scope, and compatibility model is a maintainer-owned product and security decision rather than a safe autonomous repair.

options.title: Sponsor broker-first scope
options.body: Use the manifest-declared broker as the first supported credential boundary, land it only after security and plugin API review, then evaluate a separate agent-exec consumer.

options.title: Define an agent-exec contract first
options.body: Design a narrow capability declaration and execution adapter for approved agent commands without exposing raw values through ambient environment or command text.

options.title: Keep mitigations external
options.body: Document host isolation and third-party plugins as the supported boundary and decline a core credential-use contract for agent-executed work.

recommendation.title: Sponsor broker-first scope
recommendation.body: Use the manifest-declared broker as the first supported credential boundary, land it only after security and plugin API review, then evaluate a separate agent-exec consumer.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision defines the credential isolation guarantee and security boundary across core, plugins, and agent execution.
